name: Graph RAG-Tool Fusion
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2502.07223, cs.CL); not peer-reviewed at time of record
authors_affiliation: Elias Lumer, Pradeep Honaganahalli Basavaraju, Myles Mason, James A. Burke, Vamse Kumar Subbiah - PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), AI & EmTech Teams
code_url: https://github.com/EliasLumer/Graph-RAG-Tool-Fusion-ToolLinkOS (MIT license; releases the ToolLinkOS dataset and KG schema; the dataset/benchmark rather than a full method implementation is provided)
task_domain: tool-use (tool selection / tool retrieval for LLM agents over hundreds-to-thousands of tools, APIs, or agents-as-tools)
problem_setting: Offline, retrieval-only tool selection over a predefined static tool knowledge base/graph. Single-agent tool-calling setting: given a natural-language user query, retrieve the complete set of relevant tools including their nested inter-tool dependencies so an LLM agent can execute the task. No model fine-tuning is required (plug-and-play). Evaluation is intrinsic retrieval (mAP/nDCG/Recall@k) and not end-to-end task execution; the tools are non-functional/not-runnable in both benchmarks. The tool knowledge graph is built manually offline from a schema.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool/API/agent-as-tool nodes) together with their nested dependency tools (core tools and regular tools connected by dependency edges in a tool knowledge graph)
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a predefined, manually-built tool knowledge base/graph (vector index of tool descriptions + Neo4j dependency graph). No agent-written growing/episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented: the explicit goal is to recover the COMPLETE minimal set of relevant tools plus all of their nested (direct/indirect) dependencies, not just a fixed top-k ranking. Vector search gives an initial top-k of primary tools; graph traversal then expands to recover the full dependent tool set, subject to a final top-K cap.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned as advanced RAG + knowledge-graph tool retrieval.
retrieval_unit: tool-API node (a tool/API/agent-as-tool represented as a node in a tool knowledge graph), plus KG-subgraph of its dependency tools recovered via graph traversal; effectively a tool node together with its retrieved dependency subgraph
index_source: Static corpus, offline-constructed: a predefined tool knowledge graph built manually (human-in-the-loop with LLM assistance) from a defined schema; frozen at test time (no online/test-time growth).
index_structure_topology: Hybrid of flat vector index (Azure AI Search HNSW over tool-description embeddings) AND a dependency knowledge GRAPH (Neo4j) with two node types (core tool, regular tool) and four directed dependency edge types (tool/parameter x direct/indirect). Hierarchical core-vs-regular tool distinction.
retriever_type: Hybrid: dense vector search (HNSW over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings) for first-pass tool retrieval, combined with deterministic graph traversal (depth-first search) over the dependency knowledge graph; baselines also include BM25 lexical and weighted hybrid (alpha=0.8) search. Optional LLM-as-reranker (gpt-4o).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): no fine-tuning of the retriever or embeddings; uses pretrained text-embedding-ada-002, off-the-shelf Azure AI Search (HNSW/BM25), deterministic DFS graph traversal, and a prompt-based LLM reranker. Plug-and-play, training-free.
query_construction: Raw user query is embedded for vector search; the algorithm optionally applies a query transformation function (QueryTransform, e.g. rewrite/decompose/transform) before vectorization, though the default/main experiments use the raw query without transformation.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is performed for the whole user query/instance to assemble the full tool set with dependencies.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: a single two-stage retrieval pass per query (vector search then graph traversal); no iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval during the experiments.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is invoked once per query at the start (not gated by any confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier/reflection signal).
reranking: Optional reranking stage applied to the initial top-k=3 vector-retrieved tools before graph traversal; implemented as an LLM reranker (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) with a structured (Pydantic) output schema that re-orders the candidate tool names. Reported as the 'w/ RR' variant; 'no RR' omits it.
retrieved_context_refinement: rerank (LLM reranking of the initial top-k tools) plus deterministic graph traversal expansion; final list is ordered (top vector tool then its dependencies, etc.) and truncated to a final top-K cap. No reason-in-documents distillation or distractor-filtering beyond reranking.
tool_document_engineering: Tools are indexed via their KG-schema JSON descriptions (tool name/description plus schema fields); core vs regular tool node typing and dependency edges (with 'reason' and 'parameter_name' labels) are part of the indexed representation. No synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings; raw schema/description embeddings are used for vector search.
index_content_separation: Partial: a lightweight vector index over tool descriptions is used for first-pass retrieval, while the structured dependency edges (heavy relational content) live in the Neo4j graph and are loaded on demand via traversal only for the retrieved candidate tools. Not framed as progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static, manually-built tool index (no live synchronization / CRUD auto-sync). Tools are non-functional schema-only entries; ToolSandbox tools (Python-native + selected RapidAPI) were converted into the static KG schema. No MCP/RESTful live integration in the experiments.
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes - this is the central contribution: retrieval explicitly models inter-tool dependencies via a tool knowledge graph with four edge types (tool directly/indirectly depends on; parameter directly/indirectly depends on), recovering nested dependencies (output-of-A feeds B, parameter prerequisites, OS-level/core-tool prerequisites) through DFS graph traversal up to a per-tool dependency limit (d_limit).
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the assembled top-K tool set (primary tools + their dependency tools) is equipped/provided to an LLM agent so it can call the relevant tools to solve the user query. The paper's evaluation focuses on the retrieval step itself (which tools are selected), not the downstream execution.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan / one-shot exemplars at plan time: a single retrieval pass assembles the complete dependency-aware tool set up front, which is then handed to the agent for planning/execution. Retrieval is not interleaved per-step or embedded inside a search/MCTS loop in the reported method.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-query (retrieval is performed once for the whole query, not interleaved per CoT step or per tool-call).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR/case-adaptation method; retrieved tools are passed verbatim to the agent, not adapted/revised)
retrieved_item_representation: structured tool schema entries (tool nodes with their KG-schema JSON descriptions and dependency relationships), injected as the candidate tool set / function definitions for the agent.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: tool-API level (concrete callable tool/API/agent-as-tool plus its dependency tools); not a distilled strategy, workflow, or guideline. Core tools are utility/reusable functions, regular tools are task tools.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Optional LLM reranking of the initial vector candidates to push the most relevant tool to top-1 (reducing dependency-traversal truncation and irrelevant expansions); ordering + final top-K truncation. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator. Reranking reduced truncation errors by ~52% (ToolLinkOS, mAP@10).
memory_type: graph (a static dependency knowledge graph of tools); no episodic/skill-library/procedural learned memory.
write_back: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the tool knowledge graph is built offline and is read-only at inference.
online_growth: False - the retrievable store (tool KG + vector index) is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back; the tool knowledge graph is static and pre-defined).
failure_experience_usage: N/A - no experience/failure storage; success and failure trajectories are not stored or retrieved (the system is a stateless retriever over a fixed tool graph).
memory_evolution_update: N/A - stored entries are not mutated after construction (static append-only-at-build-time graph; no online dedup/delta/refine/prune at inference).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False - retrieval/selection is fixed similarity top-k vector search plus deterministic DFS graph traversal (with an optional prompt-based LLM reranker); it is not an RL/learned retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No - single-agent, single shared static tool knowledge base; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing (though the tool KB could in principle serve multiple agents, this is not a studied dimension).
benchmarks: ToolLinkOS (new, 573 fictional tools, 1,569 instances, avg 6.3 dependencies/tool, KG schema); ToolSandbox (Lu et al. 2024; 34 tools, 1 omitted -> 33 used; 1,032 instances; converted into the GRTF KG schema).
benchmark_family: tool (tool selection / tool retrieval benchmarks). ToolLinkOS is a new dependency-rich tool-retrieval benchmark; ToolSandbox is an existing tool-use benchmark re-indexed for retrieval.
baselines: Lexical Search (BM25 via Azure AI Search / Apache Lucene); Naive RAG (dense vector search via Azure AI Search HNSW, text-embedding-ada-002) [primary comparison]; Hybrid RAG (weighted lexical+vector, alpha=0.8). GRTF variants: Graph RAG-Tool Fusion (k=3) no reranking, and (k=3) with reranking.
key_metrics: mean Average Precision (mAP) @10/@20/@30 (primary); also nDCG and Recall @10/@20/@30 in the appendix (full retrieval metrics). Reported as intrinsic retrieval-accuracy metrics.
headline_result: Graph RAG-Tool Fusion achieves absolute improvements of 71.7% and 22.1% over naive RAG on ToolLinkOS and ToolSandbox respectively (mAP@10). Concretely (mAP@10): ToolLinkOS Naive RAG 0.210 -> GRTF w/ RR 0.927 (no RR 0.856); ToolSandbox Naive RAG 0.440 -> GRTF w/ RR 0.661 (no RR 0.521). [Note: the abstract states 22.1% on ToolSandbox while the intro states 21.1%; both numbers appear in the paper - the 0.661 vs 0.440 gap is ~22.1 absolute points.]
ablations: Main ablation is reranking vs no reranking on the initial top-k=3 vector retrieval: reranking (LLM gpt-4o reranker) adds absolute +7% (ToolLinkOS) and +14% (ToolSandbox) mAP@10 over default GRTF (no RR), reaching 0.927 and 0.661. Retrieval error analysis (ToolLinkOS, k=3) decomposes errors: (1) primary tool missing from top-k vector search = 8.1% (affects both RR and no-RR equally); (2) correct tool retrieved within top-k but not top-1 then truncated = 91.6% of no-RR cases vs 43.6% of RR cases; (3) correct tool top-1 but excluded by dependency truncation = <0.01% no-RR vs 30% RR. Reranking reduced truncation errors by ~52%. Hybrid RAG vs Naive RAG vs Lexical (BM25) compares the first-pass retriever choice; the gap between Naive RAG and GRTF is much larger on the denser-dependency ToolLinkOS (6.3 deps/tool) than ToolSandbox (1.6 deps/tool), isolating graph traversal as the driver.
evaluation_decoupling: Intrinsic retrieval metrics only: the evaluation reports retrieval-quality metrics (mAP, nDCG, Recall@k) and is fully decoupled from end-to-end task/agent success - the tools are non-functional, so no downstream execution accuracy is measured.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Process/retrieval-quality metrics only (mAP/nDCG/Recall@k on tool selection); no final task-outcome (execution success) metric is reported. A retrieval error-type breakdown provides additional process-level analysis.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Framed qualitatively as 'efficient graph traversal' (DFS with a per-tool dependency limit d_limit and a final top-K cap to bound the expanded set). The retrieval-accuracy equation scales the dependency contribution by min(1, K/N). No explicit latency/API-cost/token-cost numbers or speedup measurements are reported. [uncertain on concrete cost numbers]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Two-level cut-offs: initial vector top-k=3 (and reranked top-k), per-tool dependency limit d_limit during DFS, and a final top-K cap on the assembled tool list (reranked-then-truncated). The retrieval-accuracy equation models min(1, K/N) where N is total tools discovered including dependencies; truncation of the final top-K is identified as a major error source. Specific token/prompt budget values are not given. [uncertain on exact K / d_limit values]
benchmark_construction_and_size: ToolLinkOS: 573 fictional, non-functional tools (523 regular + 50 core) across ~15 industries, avg 6.3 dependencies/tool, 1,569 query instances, with a predefined knowledge-graph schema (2 node types, 4 edge types). Constructed via human-in-the-loop iterative LLM brainstorming + dependency verification (LLMs: gpt-4o-2024-08-06, o1-2024-12-17, o1-mini-2024-09-12), with programmatic verification (3-10 deps/tool). Instances generated with gpt-4o. ToolSandbox (33 used tools, 1,032 instances, 1.6 avg deps) re-indexed into the same KG schema. Answer verifiability is via labeled relevant-tool sets for retrieval (mAP/nDCG/Recall); tools are not runnable. Best system: GRTF w/ RR reaches mAP@10 0.927 (ToolLinkOS) and 0.661 (ToolSandbox), signaling remaining difficulty on real-API-grounded ToolSandbox.
builds_on: Advanced RAG / GraphRAG (Edge et al. 2024) and knowledge-graph + LLM retrieval; dense vector retrieval (HNSW, text-embedding-ada-002) and hybrid lexical+dense retrieval (Kuzi et al. 2020); Azure AI Search (BM25/HNSW); Neo4j graph store; RAG-based tool selection/retrieval line of work (e.g., ToolBench/ToolE/Seal-Tools/ComplexFuncBench, AnyTool).
contrasts_with: Naive (vector) RAG tool retrieval, Hybrid RAG, and lexical/BM25 tool retrieval, which retrieve tools by semantic/lexical similarity alone and fail to recover semantically-unrelated but structurally-required tool dependencies; also contrasts with prior tool benchmarks (ToolBench, ToolE, Seal-Tools, ComplexFuncBench) that lack explicit tool dependencies or a KG schema.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): retrieval-augmented tool selection/retrieval for LLM agents. Positioned in the tool-retrieval sub-lineage that moves from flat vector tool retrieval toward graph/dependency-aware tool retrieval (tools-as-knowledge-graph), emphasizing dependency-completeness over top-k ranking.
